messages.author: 0a4b45fe1a09f415
messages.subject: Analyzing a series of WAV files
parts:
Hello,

I am trying to analyse a series of bird calls in WAV format using a number of functions (e.g. timer), but am having some difficulty in getting it to loop to the next after analyzing the first one. The parameters are defined as such (bolded for clarity): 

nbcalls = 48

nbindividuals = 4

individual = 1

call = 1

and the relevant lines:


for (individual in 1: nbindividuals) #number of species
{#hug1
for (call in 1: nbcalls) #number of signals
{#hug 2

#load the formula for call name
Drum_name<-paste((past1<-paste("WP_DR_",individual,sep="","_")),call,sep="",".wav")

#load the call
Drum<-readWave(Drum_name) # dois-je ajouter (silent = TRUE)?

# If the signal doesn't exist (i.e. has a length of n=1), it goes on to the next one 
if(length(Drum)==1)
{
cat("signal not found : ")
cat(" ")
cat("individual ") 
cat(individual)
cat(" call ") 
cat(call)
cat(" ? ")
cat(" Press Enter to Continue. ")
pause <- readLines(n=1)
}
else
{ #hug3
# If the signal is found, it continues on with the loop (for objects with length n > 1)
{
cat("individual") 
cat(individual)
cat("Call") 
cat(call)
cat(" Ready for Analysis! ") 
cat(" Press Enter to Continue ")
pause <- readLines(n=1)
}

}#hug 3
} #hug 2
} #hug 1

I am adapting this from a script that my advisor is letting me work with, which was designed with a previous version of Seewave. Is it possible that I am using an outdated argument to define a function? 

I should say that I am using v3.2.2 of R and v2.0.1. of Seewave on Windows 7.

Thanks for any help you may have!

--Alex

messages.subject: Re: [seewave] Analyzing a series of WAV files
parts:
Hi Alex,

I've looked into your loop, but I wasn't able to recreate your problem (i.e. I commented out the readWave section and it looped through all 48 calls for all 4 individuals).

I tried formatting it in the 'standard' R format (below), which might make it a bit easier. Possibly this is the problem on your system? Also, you don't need to define call and individual before hand (but it doesn't matter that you have).

Good luck! Let me know how it goes!

Steffi

##number of species
for (individual in 1: nbindividuals) {
    #number of signals
    for (call in 1: nbcalls) { 
        #load the formula for call name
        Drum_name<-paste((past1<-paste("WP_DR_",individual,sep="","_")),call,sep="",".wav")

        #load the call
        #Drum<-readWave(Drum_name) # dois-je ajouter (silent = TRUE)?
        Drum <- 1
        # If the signal doesn't exist (i.e. has a length of n=1), it goes on to the next one 
        if(length(Drum)==1) {
            cat("signal not found : ")
            cat(" ")
            cat("individual ")
            cat(individual)
            cat(" call ")
            cat(call)
            cat(" ? ")
            cat(" Press Enter to Continue. ")
            pause <- readLines(n=1)
    } else {
            # If the signal is found, it continues on with the loop (for objects with length n > 1)
            cat("individual")
            cat(individual)
            cat("Call")
            cat(call)
            cat(" Ready for Analysis! ")
            cat(" Press Enter to Continue ")
            pause <- readLines(n=1)
        }
    }
}
